relevance_note: The paper describes three named patients with Tangier disease and their relatives with individual-level details: "Three patients homozygous for Tangier disease (A. Bo., a 56-yr-old man; J. Si., a 42-yr-old man; and E. Ga., a 46-yr-old woman, sister of J. Si.)"; no ABCA1 variant is printed.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown by hand; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and copied the three Table I rows (patient label through all four cells) verbatim from the file. The paper (1976-77, before the gene was known) names no gene and prints no ABCA1 variant, so the variants table is empty; 'homozygous for Tangier disease' and 'obligate heterozygote' are disease-level statements without a variant. The year of publication is not printed (only 'Received for publication 26 July 1976'), so year is null. n_patients_reported counts the three diagnosed Tangier patients (none has a printed variant). The PDF-to-text conversion is garbled and out of order in places: (1) an unattributed paragraph ('Tonsillectomy was performed at age 20 yr ... hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, flocculent infiltration throughout the corneal stroma, and recurrent polyneuropathy ... lamina propria of the colonic mucosa') sits between the Methods patient list and the A. Bo. section without naming a patient; by elimination it is probably A. Bo. (J. Si. tonsillectomy at 37, E. Ga. at 9), but the paper does not say so, so it was NOT attributed to anyone (corneal opacity, neuropathy, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, tonsillectomy left not reported for A. Bo.). (2) The paragraph 'In the patient's children (16-yr-old boy; 14-yr-old girl)' follows the E. Ga. section, but E. Ga.'s children are stated as 9, 4 and 3 yr and A. Bo. has an 'only daughter'; Fig. 1 refers to obligate heterozygote 'children of J. Si. and E. Ga.' (sera 6-10, five sera), so these two are probably J. Si.'s children, but the parent is not stated; they are labelled 'unnamed person 1' and 'unnamed person 2' rather than attributed. Their paired lipid values ('110 and 115', '225 and 170', '15 and 18') were not assigned to each child by position; only the group-level HDL deficiency statement was used. (3) Text about the pharyngeal/tonsillar tags of J. Si. ('orange-Yels  ol i l  e  a mec tion') and E. Ga. ('ans e-s  nno  uy s l tags on the pharynx were visible') is garbled, so orange-colored tonsils was left not reported for both. Children of E. Ga.: their ages (9, 4, 3 yr) were assigned to labels in order of mention; the lipid findings come from the group statement 'in these children' and their disease label and 'diminished HDL reactivity' from the Fig. 1 legend naming 'children of J. Si. and E. Ga.'. A. Bo.'s daughter: only raw values (cholesterol 120–140, HDL cholesterol 20-22 mg/100 ml) are given without the paper calling them abnormal, so no feature rows. A. Bo.'s triglycerides 'at or near 100 mg/100 ml' were not called normal by the paper, so hypertriglyceridemia is not reported for him. J. Si.: 'Careful neurological examination was negative' is recorded as an excluded 'abnormal neurological examination' only; under D-27 it does not exclude peripheral neuropathy, reduced tendon reflexes or reduced deep sensation. Lipid storage in Schwann cells is histology and was not taken as clinical peripheral neuropathy. 'Absence of HDL' on lipoprotein analysis was taken as low HDL cholesterol. Low apoprotein A-I rests on each patient's Table I row plus the text naming 'all Tangier patients'. Table II (distribution percentages) was not used for features. No contradictions within the paper were found.
